outcome: type and indications of cesarean section
cohort: A total of 240 women delivering at a tertiary care center were included, with 120 deliveries each during the pre-COVID and COVID periods.
finding: The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with a significant surge in cesarean section deliveries, earlier gestational age at birth, lower neonatal birth weight, and increased NICU admissions.
mod_finding: The cesarean section rate increased significantly from 35.0% in the pre-COVID period to 56.7% during the COVID period.
cross-section timing: Comparison between pre-COVID and COVID periods
birth_weight: Significantly lower during the COVID period (specific weights not provided for both groups, only stated as lower)
gest_age: Significantly lower during the COVID period (37.4 +/- 1.9 weeks) compared to pre-COVID (38.1 +/- 1.6 weeks)
